metadata.note: The semantic colour layer. Palettes live in themes/bundled/*.theme.json; this file says what each palette entry is FOR, and is the only place a derivation is written. A role's `from` names a theme manifest key; the CSS variable that key writes to is derived (kebab-case), not tabulated. See COLOR.md.

text-disabled.note: disabled non-control text = the default text colour at the `strong` (60%) alpha step — a disabled element inherits its enabled semantic colour, dimmed at the token level, never a dedicated disabled palette value

text-link.note: global.css `a {}` is the only consumer; no component styles a bare link

container-workspace-bg.note: the app surface, and with it the opened-document canvas — a document reads as part of the workspace (Monaco's EDITOR_THEME, the markdown/spec preview, the chat column, the tab strip)

container-content-bg.note: the recessed read-a-diff/read-code canvas, NOT the document canvas (that is workspace): the Changes diff (Monaco THEME), rendered diffs, Shiki code blocks, and the center-column backdrop behind them

container-elevated-bg.note: every raised surface: dialogs, popovers, menus, toasts, cards, code blocks

control-primary-bg.note: the SOLID primary button fill — its own palette source (`accentSolid`), decoupled from `accent` so a theme can brighten the opaque fill without moving the alpha-derived primary tints (primary-subtle/soft/muted) or the accent used for text/ring/border; every theme maps accentSolid to its accent except regular Light, which uses the brighter dark-theme green

control-primary-bg-hovered.note: the primary button's hover fill — its own manifest key so a theme owns the hover step instead of the button fading with an opacity utility

control-disabled-bg.note: disabled control fill = the default control fill (`input`, i.e. control-bg) at the `strong` (60%) alpha step

control-disabled-text.note: disabled control label/icon = the default control text colour (`text`, i.e. text-default) at the `strong` (60%) alpha step

control-disabled-border.note: disabled control border = the default control border (`border`, i.e. control-border-default) at the `strong` (60%) alpha step

control-primary-disabled-bg.note: disabled primary button fill = the accent hue at the `strong` (60%) alpha step — kept on `accent` (the alpha-tint base), not the brightened solid `accentSolid`, so the disabled fill stays with the primary tint family

control-primary-disabled-text.note: disabled primary button label/icon = the normal primary text (`onAccent`, i.e. control-primary-text) at the `strong` (60%) alpha step

selection-text.note: nullable in the manifest (high contrast keeps the native foreground)

selection-bg.note: native ::selection in global.css; not a utility

selection-bg-muted.note: the content canvas's ::selection (markdown preview): translucent, so the unselected remainder of a line box reads as a soft edge, not a black hole punched in an opaque wash

editor-selection-text.note: read by Monaco and xterm through getComputedStyle; a utility would be dead weight
